subject: Barcelona workshop: embassy packet, supporting affidavit, and passport lead times
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gómez <marta.gomez@acmesoft.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Barcelona workshop: embassy packet, supporting affidavit, and passport lead times

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for hosting the executive workshop in Barcelona (Mar 9–11). We're consolidating documents for our execs and need to confirm a few embassy/visa logistics so there are no delays. Quick ask below; I pasted Rishi for passport coordination.

Required items from Redwood side (we can provide these within 72 hours once you confirm):
- Invitation/support letter for each attendee (PDF, signed) — please confirm preferred wording/recipient name format (first + last as in passport).
- Company registration + proof of business purpose (we've attached our standard support letter as a starting point).
- Suggested consulate contact or mail pickup option for Schengen short-stay business visas.

Attendee passport constraints (we will collect scans):
- Passport must be valid for at least 90 days beyond return date (we generally require 6 months, but Spain enforces 90 days).
- No more than 2 blank visa pages recommended.

Timeline we're working to:
- 2026-01-13: collect passport scans from all attendees
- 2026-01-16: invitation/support letter finalized and shared with consulate if needed
- 2026-01-20: ship hard copies of letters (courier) to your HQ for consulate submission

Can you confirm:
1) Who at AcmeSoft will submit to the consulate on our behalf (name + email)?
2) If the consulate requires an apostille or legalized version for corporate docs?
3) Whether your team can accept a courier package arriving 2 business days before submission?

Attachments: redwood-barcelona-support-letter.pdf (draft), attendee-passport-table.csv (we'll populate).

If anything on the list looks off, flag it — we can adapt wording.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

--

On Mon, 12 Jan 2026 at 09:12, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Marta —
> 
> Thanks again for hosting the executive workshop in Barcelona (Mar 9–11). We're consolidating documents for our execs and need to confirm a few embassy/visa logistics so there are no delays. Quick ask below; I pasted Rishi for passport coordination.

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear list. I can act as the onsite liaison and submit the packet to the consulate if needed. A few notes from our side:

- Preferred invitation wording: full name + passport number on the PDF is helpful; we can add business purpose language. If you can confirm name format by EOD Wednesday (local), we'll include passport numbers when you provide them.
- Apostille: Spanish consulates do not accept apostilles for corporate support letters for short-stay business visas; however, some districts ask for notarization. I'll check with the consulate rep and update.
- Courier: we can receive a package up to 3 business days before submission — please include tracking and customs invoice.

I will follow up with the specific consulate contact and whether they need translated documents. Also attaching a preliminary consulate contact list.

Regards,
Marta Gómez
Head of Events, AcmeSoft
Marta.Gomez@acmesoft.com | +34 93 555 2244

Vanessa / Marta —

Thanks — quick updates from my side after checking with HR and the exec assistants:

- We'll have scans for all six executives by EOD 2026-01-13. I'll upload to the shared Drive (secure folder) and then send you the attendee-passport-table.csv completed.
- Two execs (A. Chen and M. Lin) will need expedited handling — passports expire May 2026; consulate advised early submissions. We'll use overnight courier for their packets.
- For signatures on the support letters, can we do DocuSign? I can trigger two envelopes today once you confirm final wording.

On the apostille/notarization question: if the consulate requires notarized corporate docs, we can arrange local notarization and include the notary slip in the packet — that will add 2–3 business days.

I'll coordinate the courier pickup once Marta confirms the receiving address and any special customs details.

Thanks,
